# **RNA-sequencing analysis**
### Bulk RNA-sequencing of ingWAT RNA from FGF21 supplementd and CHX tumor-bearing animals 
#### **Experiment TO302-354**


This workflow contains data analysis of differential expressed gene (DEG) data. 
The initial measurements and primary analysis (EdgeR) of this project was done by TAmiRNA GmbH.

We start with loading all the EdgeR data containing gene names, log Fold changes, FDR (substitutes the adjusted p-value) for each contrast between two different contitions.
At the end, we save all the data frames we just loaded in one project data file. 

Before you begin, make sure that all your required packages are installed - you can do this by:
"install.package(*package name*)" or with the help of BiocManager::install()

```{r, load data}

files <- c(
  Efruxi_CHX  = here::here(datadir,
    "Condition#Tumor&Treatment#Efruxifermin_vs_Condition#Tumor&Treatment#untreated_edgeRResults.xlsx"),
  AAV_CHX = here::here(datadir,
    "Condition#Tumor&Treatment#FGF21_AAV_vs_Condition#Tumor&Treatment#untreated_edgeRResults.xlsx"),
  CHX_healthy = here::here(datadir,
    "Condition#Tumor&Treatment#untreated_vs_Condition#Healthy&Treatment#untreated_edgeRResults.xlsx"),
  Efruxi_HC = here::here(datadir,
    "Condition#Tumor&Treatment#Efruxifermin_vs_Condition#Healthy&Treatment#untreated_edgeRResults.xlsx"),
  AAV_HC = here::here(datadir,
    "Condition#Tumor&Treatment#FGF21_AAV_vs_Condition#Healthy&Treatment#untreated_edgeRResults.xlsx"),
  Efruxi_AAV = here::here(datadir,
    "Condition#Tumor&Treatment#Efruxifermin_vs_Condition#Tumor&Treatment#FGF21_AAV_edgeRResults.xlsx"))
data <- lapply(files, rio::import, trust = TRUE)

Efruxi_CHX <- data$Efruxi_CHX
AAV_CHX <- data$AAV_CHX
CHX_healthy <- data$CHX_healthy
Efruxi_HC <- data$Efruxi_HC
AAV_HC <- data$AAV_HC
Efruxi_AAV <- data$Efruxi_AAV

save(Efruxi_AAV, AAV_CHX, AAV_HC, Efruxi_CHX, Efruxi_HC, CHX_healthy, file = "RNASeq_edgeR_data.RData")

```


### **Venn diagrams** of DEGs

Next we will visualize the DEGs of the different contrasts first by dropping all non-significant genes.
For this, we will use a logFC of at least 1 (2-fold increase) and a FDR of at least 0.05 (similar to adjusted p-value which is mostly Benjamini-Hochberg corrected).


```{r, filter DEGs}
library(dplyr)
library(ggvenn)

# Optional: either continue or load data
#load("RNASeq_edgeR_data.RData")

# set filter thresholds
logFC_cutoff <- 1
FDR_cutoff <- 0.05


# select genes meeting the filters, up and down individually
sig_genes <- function(data) {
  up <- data %>% filter(logFC >= logFC_cutoff, FDR < FDR_cutoff) %>% pull(external_gene_name)
  down <- data %>% filter(logFC <= -logFC_cutoff, FDR < FDR_cutoff) %>% pull(external_gene_name)

  # ensures empty sets are character 0
  if(length(up) == 0) up <- character(0)
  if(length(down) == 0) down <- character(0)
  # for up, down and combined entries
  list(up = unique(up), 
       down = unique(down),
       all = unique(c(up, down)))
}


# for individual rows with up, down and combined
sig_Efruxi_CHX <- sig_genes(Efruxi_CHX)
sig_AAV_CHX <- sig_genes(AAV_CHX)
sig_CHX_HC <- sig_genes(CHX_healthy)
sig_Efruxi_HC <- sig_genes(Efruxi_HC)
sig_AAV_HC <- sig_genes(AAV_HC)
sig_Efruxi_AAV <- sig_genes(Efruxi_AAV)

# you can display the lists by:
head(sig_Efruxi_CHX)



# combine all contrasts
sig_all_contrasts <- cbind(sig_Efruxi_CHX, 
                           sig_AAV_CHX, 
                           sig_CHX_HC, 
                           sig_Efruxi_HC, 
                           sig_AAV_HC,
                           sig_Efruxi_AAV)


# significant up DEGs for each contrast
up_genes <- list(Efruxi_CHX = sig_Efruxi_CHX$up,
                 AAV_CHX = sig_AAV_CHX$up,
                 CHX_HC = sig_CHX_HC$up,
                 Efruxi_HC = sig_Efruxi_HC$up,
                 AAV_HC = sig_AAV_HC$up,
                 Efruxi_AAV = sig_Efruxi_AAV$up)

# significant down genes for each contrast
down_genes <- list(Efruxi_CHX = sig_Efruxi_CHX$down,
                 AAV_CHX = sig_AAV_CHX$down,
                 CHX_HC = sig_CHX_HC$down,
                 Efruxi_HC = sig_Efruxi_HC$down,
                 AAV_HC = sig_AAV_HC$down,
                 Efruxi_AAV = sig_Efruxi_AAV$down)


```


### Venn Diagrams

Now you have all the **differential expressed genes in lists** for each contrast. 

If you want to visualize intersections, you can continue with **Venn diagrams**. 
This does not only give you a nice diagram but also the amount of common genes between your comparisons and the percentage of all genes is this intersection. 

I like to stick with one color scheme for one project. You can change the color scheme either by applying different color scheme packages or by changing the hardcoded colors according to your linking. Here are some webpages for color inspirations:

- https://sape.inf.usi.ch/quick-reference/ggplot2/colour
- https://derekogle.com/NCGraphing/resources/colors
- https://www.nceas.ucsb.edu/sites/default/files/2020-04/colorPaletteCheatsheet.pdf



```{r Venns}

### Treated Tumor DEGs + untreated Tumor DEGs ###
# intersection list for venn - up genes
up_genes_venn <- list(Efruxi_CHX = sig_Efruxi_CHX$up,
                 AAV_CHX = sig_AAV_CHX$up,
                 CHX_HC = sig_CHX_HC$up)

# intersection list for venn - down genes
down_genes_venn <- list(Efruxi_CHX = sig_Efruxi_CHX$down,
                        AAV_CHX = sig_AAV_CHX$down,
                        CHX_HC = sig_CHX_HC$down)

# venn diagram
ggvenn(up_genes_venn,
       fill_color = c("lightslateblue", "maroon3", "gray77"),
       fill_alpha = 0.4,
       stroke_size = 0.1,
       set_name_size = 3,
       text_size = 3,
       show_percentage = TRUE)+
  ggtitle("Overlap of Upregulated Genes") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10))



# intersection list for venn - intersection DEGs Treatments
treatments_DEGs_genes_venn <- list(Efruxi_CHX = sig_Efruxi_CHX$up,
                                  AAV_CHX = sig_AAV_CHX$up,
                                  Efruxi_CHX = sig_Efruxi_CHX$down,
                                  AAV_CHX = sig_AAV_CHX$down)
# venn diagram
plot <- ggvenn(treatments_DEGs_genes_venn,
       fill_color = c("lightslateblue", "maroon3"),
       fill_alpha = 0.4,
       stroke_size = 0.1,
       set_name_size = 5,
       text_size = 6,
       show_percentage = TRUE)+
  ggtitle("Overlap of Diff. regulated Genes_treatments") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10))

plot
# save plot
#ggsave("VENN_DEGs_treatments_600dpi.tiff", plot, dpi = 600)



# intersection DEGs of up in treated vs down in untreated (12 DEGs)
common_intersection <- Reduce(intersect, list(sig_Efruxi_CHX$up, sig_AAV_CHX$up, sig_CHX_HC$down))
# get intersection genes of AAVvsCHX and EfruxivsCHX
common_up_DEGs_treatments <- Reduce(intersect, list(sig_Efruxi_CHX$up, sig_AAV_CHX$up))
common_down_DEGs_treatments <- Reduce(intersect, list(sig_Efruxi_CHX$down, sig_AAV_CHX$down))



# export data

#sig_all_contrasts %>% 
#  rio::export(here::here(datadir, "significant_DEGs_all_contrasts.RDS"))
#up_genes_venn %>% 
#  rio::export(here::here(datadir, "up_genes_treatments_CHX.RDS"))
#down_genes_venn %>% 
#  rio::export(here::here(datadir, "down_genes_treatments_CHX.RDS"))
#common_up_DEGs_treatments %>% 
#  rio::export(here::here(datadir, "DEGs_treatments_92.RDS"))
#common_intersection %>%

```


## Heatmaps
### Heatmap of DEG group means

Of course, you can represent your seq-data also in a **heatmap** format. 
You can do this either of the whole seq data or in a specific subset of your choice.

For this we take the "Reads per million" table containing a normalized gene expression matrix, where raw read counts are scaled by the total number of mapped reads in each sample. For this heatmap we will take the mean of the respicates per group. 
We first define a subset that is of high interest (e.g. all DEGs between healthy vs untreated tumor-bearing mice "sig_CHX_HC$all").
Then we restructure our data frame to obtain the required format, then we preprocess the data by log transformation and z-scaling to handle skewed data and represent it better on a comparable scale. 

With the "pheatmap" package you can also cluster rows and columns. Meaning that R performs hierarchical clustering by default to group similar data points and displays them in dendrograms. Be aware that clustering can also change the order of your data displayed.



```{r, Heatmaps of DEGs}
library(dplyr)
library(pheatmap)

#import data
rpm_mat <- rio::import(here::here(datadir, "genesRPMTable.xlsx"), trust = TRUE)
# determine genes to be filtered
genes_of_interest <- sig_CHX_HC$all
# filter genes of interest
rpm_sub <- rpm_mat %>%
  dplyr::filter(external_gene_name %in% genes_of_interest)
# check intersection of genes 
intersect(genes_of_interest, rpm_mat$external_gene_name)

# annotate groups
count_cols <- grep("^\\d+_", colnames(rpm_sub), value = TRUE)
#count_cols
length(count_cols)

groups <- sub("^\\d+_", "", count_cols)
#groups
table(groups)


# sample annotation
sample_info <- data.frame(sample = count_cols,
                          group = groups,
                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# prepare matrix, subtract all descriptive columns
rpm_sub <- rpm_sub %>%
  dplyr::select(-description) %>%
  dplyr::select(-gene) %>%
  dplyr::select(external_gene_name, all_of(count_cols))

rpm_sub <- rpm_sub %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("external_gene_name")
  
# mean per groups
rpm_mean <- sapply(
  split(seq_along(groups), groups),
  function(idx) rowMeans(rpm_sub[, idx, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE))

# log transform
rpm_sub_log <- log2(rpm_mean + 1)
# z scale
rpm_sub_scaled <- t(scale(t(rpm_sub_log)))

# order groups 
group_order <- c("healthy", "CHX", "AAV", "Efruxi")
rpm_sub_scaled <- rpm_sub_scaled[, group_order]


# define legend color breaks
min <- min(-1.5)
max <- max(1.5)

# Make color breaks so that 0 is white
n_colors <- 100
breaks <- c(
  seq(min, 0, length.out = n_colors/2 + 1),
  seq(0, max, length.out = n_colors/2 + 1)[-1]
)

heatmap <- pheatmap(
  rpm_sub_scaled,
  main = paste("DEGs CHXvsHC_all groups"),
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  color = colorRampPalette(c("navy","white","firebrick3"))(n_colors),
  cellwidth = 10,
  cellheight = 10,
  fontsize_row = 9,
  fontsize_col = 9,
  breaks = breaks)

#ggsave("heatmap_DEGs_CHXvsHC.tiff", heatmap, dpi = 600, width = 5, height = 12)


```


And one example for the DEG intersection of different groups (e.g. up in EFX_vs_CHX and up in AAV_vs_CHX).


```{r, Heatmaps of DEG intersections}
library(pheatmap)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)



# load data
treatment_DEGs_92 <- rio::import(here::here(datadir, "DEGs_treatments_92.RDS"), trust = TRUE)
treatment_DEGs_unique_80 <- rio::import(here::here(datadir, "unique_DEGs_treatments_80.RDS"), trust = TRUE)

common_intersection_12 <- as.data.frame(common_intersection_12)
colnames(common_intersection_12)[1] <- "external_gene_name"
treatment_DEGs_unique_80 <- as.data.frame(treatment_DEGs_unique_80)
colnames(treatment_DEGs_unique_80)[1] <- "external_gene_name"

colnames(treatment_DEGs_92)[1] <- "external_gene_name"




#import data
rpm_mat <- rio::import(here::here(datadir, "genesRPMTable.xlsx"), trust = TRUE)
# determine genes to be filtered

genes_of_interest <- genes_of_interest$external_gene_name
# filter genes of interest
rpm_sub <- rpm_mat %>%
  dplyr::filter(external_gene_name %in% genes_of_interest)
# check intersection of genes 
intersect(genes_of_interest, rpm_mat$external_gene_name)

# annotate groups
count_cols <- grep("^\\d+_", colnames(rpm_sub), value = TRUE)
#count_cols
length(count_cols)

groups <- sub("^\\d+_", "", count_cols)
#groups
table(groups)


# sample annotation
sample_info <- data.frame(sample = count_cols,
                          group = groups,
                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# prepare matrix, subtract all descriptive columns
rpm_sub <- rpm_sub %>%
  dplyr::select(-description) %>%
  dplyr::select(-gene) %>%
  dplyr::select(external_gene_name, all_of(count_cols))

rpm_sub <- rpm_sub %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("external_gene_name")
  
# mean per groups
rpm_mean <- sapply(
  split(seq_along(groups), groups),
  function(idx) rowMeans(rpm_sub[, idx, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE))

# log transform
rpm_sub_log <- log2(rpm_mean + 1)
# z scale
rpm_sub_scaled <- t(scale(t(rpm_sub_log)))

# order groups 
group_order <- c("healthy", "CHX", "AAV", "Efruxi")
rpm_sub_scaled <- rpm_sub_scaled[, group_order]


# define legend color breaks
min <- min(-1.5)
max <- max(1.5)

# Make color breaks so that 0 is white
n_colors <- 100
breaks <- c(
  seq(min, 0, length.out = n_colors/2 + 1),
  seq(0, max, length.out = n_colors/2 + 1)[-1]
)

heatmap <- pheatmap(
  rpm_sub_scaled,
  main = paste("DEGs- 92 intersection"),
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  treeheight_row = 15,
  color = colorRampPalette(c("navy","white","firebrick3"))(n_colors),
  cellwidth = 9,
  cellheight = 7,
  fontsize_row = 8,
  fontsize_col = 7,
  breaks = breaks)
heatmap
#ggsave("heatmap_DEGs_92_intersection.tiff", heatmap, dpi = 600, width = 6, height= 14)
```

### Heatmap of gene sets

And of course you can also do this for target gene sets. These can be either customized or downloaded as .gmt files for instance. 
Best gene set source is msigDB which you might already know from GSEA. Be careful that you select the correct species!

- https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/msigdb/mouse/collections.jsp

This first snippet creates heatmaps for all replicates.

```{r, Heatmaps of genesets, individual}
library(dplyr)
library(pheatmap)
library(ggrepel)
library(tibble)

#import data
rpm_mat <- rio::import(here::here(datadir, "genesRPMTable.xlsx"), trust = TRUE)

# determine group names
group_levels <- c("Healthy", "CHX", "AAV", "Efruxi")

# define regex pattern
pattern <- "^(.*?)_?(\\d+)_(healthy|chx|aav|efruxi)$"

# get colnames and align against regex
cn <- colnames(rpm_mat)
sample_cols <- cn[grepl(pattern, cn, ignore.case = TRUE)]

grp_raw <- tolower(sub(pattern, "\\3", sample_cols, ignore.case = TRUE))


sample_info <- data.frame(
  sample   = sample_cols,
  celltype = sub(pattern, "\\1", sample_cols, ignore.case = TRUE),
  animal   = sub(pattern, "\\2", sample_cols, ignore.case = TRUE),
  group    = factor(group_levels[match(grp_raw, tolower(group_levels))],
                    levels = group_levels),
  row.names = sample_cols)
table(sample_info$celltype, sample_info$group)


# Load geneset data
gmt <- here::here(datadir, "paper_geneset.gmt")
gmt_inflamm_resp <- readLines(gmt) %>%
  strsplit("\t") %>%
  lapply(function(x) x[-c(1, 2)]) %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unique()

# filter gene subset included in geneset
mat <- rpm_mat %>%
  filter(external_gene_name %in% gmt_inflamm_resp) %>%
  distinct(external_gene_name, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(external_gene_name, all_of(sample_cols)) %>%
  column_to_rownames("external_gene_name") %>%
  as.matrix()

mat <- mat[intersect(gmt_inflamm_resp, rownames(mat)), , drop = FALSE]

mat_log <- log2(mat + 1)
nrow(mat_log); length(gmt_inflamm_resp) 



### 1. For individual samples ### 
  
# for individual samples
plot_indiv_heatmap <- function(samples, title, file = NULL, lim = 2) {
  m <- mat_log[, samples, drop = FALSE]
  m <- m[apply(m, 1, sd, na.rm = TRUE) > 0, , drop = FALSE]    # drop flat genes
  m <- t(scale(t(m)))
  m <- pmax(pmin(m, lim), -lim)

  ann_col    <- sample_info[samples, "group", drop = FALSE]
  ann_colors <- list(group = c(Healthy = "black", CHX = "grey75",
                  AAV = "maroon", Efruxi = "#9FA3FF"))

  n_colors <- 100
  breaks <- c(seq(-lim, 0, length.out = n_colors/2 + 1),
              seq(0, lim, length.out = n_colors/2 + 1)[-1])

  ph <- pheatmap(m, main = title,
                 cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = FALSE,
                 color = colorRampPalette(c("navy", "white", "firebrick3"))(n_colors),
                 breaks = breaks,
                 annotation_col = ann_col, annotation_colors = ann_colors,
                 cellwidth = 14, cellheight = 10, fontsize_row = 9,
                 silent = TRUE)
  grid::grid.newpage(); grid::grid.draw(ph$gtable)
  if (!is.null(file))
    ggplot2::ggsave(file, ph$gtable, dpi = 600, bg = "white",
                    width = 1.5 + length(samples) * 14 / 72 + 2,
                    height = nrow(m) * 10 / 72 + 2.5)
  invisible(ph)
}

# plot
plot_indiv_heatmap(sample_info %>% 
                   arrange(group) %>% 
                   pull(sample),
                   "paper_geneset.gmt",
                   "heatmap_paper_geneset.tiff")

```


Or you can do this also for the mean of each group replicate as before. 
Be aware that you lose specificity when you take the mean instead of your individual replicates. 



```{r Heatmaps of genesets, mean}
### 2. For mean per celltypes ###

# z scores of all samples per condition

mean_by_group <- function(groups) {
  sapply(groups, function(g) {
    rowMeans(mat_log[, sample_info$group == g, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  })
}


plot_mean_heatmap <- function(title, file = NULL, lim = 1.5) {
  groups <- levels(sample_info$group)
  m <- mean_by_group(groups)
  m <- m[apply(m, 1, sd, na.rm = TRUE) > 0, , drop = FALSE]    # drop flat genes
  m <- t(scale(t(m)))
  m <- pmax(pmin(m, lim), -lim)
  
  ann_col <- data.frame(group = factor(colnames(m), levels = groups),
                           row.names = colnames(m))
  ann_colors <- list(group = c(Healthy = "black", CHX = "grey75",
                  AAV = "maroon", Efruxi = "#9FA3FF"))

  n_colors <- 100
  breaks <- c(seq(-lim, 0, length.out = n_colors/2 + 1),
              seq(0, lim, length.out = n_colors/2 + 1)[-1])

  ph <- pheatmap(m, main = title,
                 cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = FALSE,
                 color = colorRampPalette(c("navy", "white", "firebrick3"))(n_colors),
                 breaks = breaks,
                 annotation_col = ann_col, annotation_colors = ann_colors,
                 #gaps_col = seq(2, ncol(m) - 1, by = 2),    # gap between cell types
                 cellwidth = 20, cellheight = 10, fontsize_row = 9, silent = TRUE)
  grid::grid.newpage(); grid::grid.draw(ph$gtable)
  if (!is.null(file))
    ggplot2::ggsave(file, ph$gtable, dpi = 600, bg = "white",
                    width = 2 + ncol(m) * 20 / 72 + 2,
                    height = nrow(m) * 10 / 72 + 2.5)
  invisible(ph)
}


plot_mean_heatmap("paper_geneset.gmt",
                  "heatmap_paper_geneset_mean.tiff")


```




### Cytoscape and Wikipathway

This code prepares your data frames for specific Wikipathways similar to gene set referencing.
You can import your Wikipathway of interest as .csv and align the egene expression of your dataset.

The visual representation, however is done with cytoscape. 
You can download the created dataframes which are suitable for cytoscape and apply them for pathway alignment and design. 

- https://www.wikipathways.org/
- https://cytoscape.org/


```{r, Cytoscape + Wikipathways}
library(dplyr)



### prepare Data for cytoscape
load("RNASeq_edgeR_data.RData")

df_1 <- CHX_healthy
df_2 <- AAV_CHX
df_3 <- Efruxi_CHX

# function filter columns 
prep_df <- function(df, suffix) {
  df %>% 
    select(gene, external_gene_name, logFC, FDR) %>%
    rename_with(~paste0(., "_", suffix), c(logFC, FDR))
}

CHXvsHC_clean <- prep_df(df_1, "CHXvsHC")
AAVvsCHX_clean <- prep_df(df_2, "AAVvsCHX")
EfruxivsCHX_clean <- prep_df(df_3, "EfruxivsCHX")

# 3. Alle drei Tabellen über die Ensembl-ID (gene) zusammenführen
master_table <- CHXvsHC_clean %>%
  full_join(AAVvsCHX_clean, by = c("gene", "external_gene_name")) %>%
  full_join(EfruxivsCHX_clean, by = c("gene", "external_gene_name"))



### load Wikipathway data and check for completeness in RNASeq data

### WP2316 PPAR Signalling
WPathway <- rio::import(here::here(datadir, "pparg-signaling_Mm.csv"), trust = TRUE)
# filter for genes only
WPathway_genes <- WPathway %>%
  filter(Type == "GeneProduct")


# check how many genes from WPathway are present in edgeR DEG data
comparison <- WPathway_genes %>%
  dplyr::select(name, Type, XrefId, XrefDatasource) %>%
  left_join(master_table, by = c("name" = "external_gene_name"))

found <- sum(!is.na(comparison$logFC_CHXvsHC))
total <- nrow(comparison)
percent <- (found/total)*100
message(paste0("Found: ", found, " of ", total, " genes (", round(percent, 2), "%)"))
# which genes are missing
missing_genes <- comparison %>%
  filter(is.na(logFC_CHXvsHC)) %>%
  select(name)
print(missing_genes)

comparison_for_cytoscape <- comparison %>%
  mutate(
    Chart_Data = paste(logFC_CHXvsHC, logFC_AAVvsCHX, logFC_EfruxivsCHX, sep = ","),
    Visual_Instructions = paste0("charts: bar: data=\"", Chart_Data, "\" colorlist=\"blue,white,red\" range=\"-5,5\""))
comparison_for_cytoscape <- comparison_for_cytoscape %>%
  mutate(Chart_Data_Clean = gsub("NA", "0.0", Chart_Data),
         Visual_Instructions = paste0("charts: bar: data=\"", Chart_Data_Clean, 
                                 "\" colorlist=\"blue,white,red\" range=\"-5,5\""))

rio::export(comparison_for_cytoscape, here::here(resultsdir, "Cytoscape_Final_Charts_WP2316.csv"))




### WP2872 White fat cell differentiation
WPathway <- rio::import(here::here(datadir, "White_fat_cell_differentiation_Mm.csv"), trust = TRUE)
# filter for genes only
WPathway_genes <- WPathway %>%
  filter(Type == "GeneProduct")


# check how many genes from WPathway are present in edgeR DEG data
comparison <- WPathway_genes %>%
  dplyr::select(name, Type, XrefId, XrefDatasource) %>%
  left_join(master_table, by = c("name" = "external_gene_name"))

found <- sum(!is.na(comparison$logFC_CHXvsHC))
total <- nrow(comparison)
percent <- (found/total)*100
message(paste0("Found: ", found, " of ", total, " genes (", round(percent, 2), "%)"))
# which genes are missing
missing_genes <- comparison %>%
  filter(is.na(logFC_CHXvsHC)) %>%
  select(name)
print(missing_genes)

comparison_for_cytoscape <- comparison %>%
  mutate(
    Chart_Data = paste(logFC_CHXvsHC, logFC_AAVvsCHX, logFC_EfruxivsCHX, sep = ","),
    Visual_Instructions = paste0("charts: bar: data=\"", Chart_Data, "\" colorlist=\"blue,white,red\" range=\"-5,5\""))
comparison_for_cytoscape <- comparison_for_cytoscape %>%
  mutate(Chart_Data_Clean = gsub("NA", "0.0", Chart_Data),
         Visual_Instructions = paste0("charts: bar: data=\"", Chart_Data_Clean, 
                                 "\" colorlist=\"blue,white,red\" range=\"-5,5\""))

rio::export(comparison_for_cytoscape, here::here(resultsdir, "Cytoscape_Final_Charts_WP2872.csv"))



WP2872 <- rio::import(here::here(resultsdir, "Cytoscape_Final_Charts_WP2872.csv"))
```

### PPARg target genes

This code focuses on filtering the publicly available PPARg target gene lists for confidence levels and species. 
The filteres target genes are then aligned to the DEG data and visualized by Venn diagrams.

- https://www.ppargene.org/



```{r, Pparg target filter}
library(dplyr)
library(biomaRt)
library(ggplot2)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)

# load data
treatment_DEGs_92 <- rio::import(here::here(datadir, "DEGs_treatments_92.RDS"), trust = TRUE)
treatment_DEGs_unique_80 <- rio::import(here::here(datadir, "unique_DEGs_treatments_80.RDS"), trust = TRUE)
common_intersection_12 <- rio::import(here::here(datadir, "DEGs_treatments_CHX_common_12.RDS"), trust = TRUE)

common_intersection_12 <- as.data.frame(common_intersection_12)
colnames(common_intersection_12)[1] <- "GeneSymbol"
treatment_DEGs_unique_80 <- as.data.frame(treatment_DEGs_unique_80)
colnames(treatment_DEGs_unique_80)[1] <- "GeneSymbol"
treatment_DEGs_92 <- data.frame(value = unlist(treatment_DEGs_92))
colnames(treatment_DEGs_92)[1] <- "GeneSymbol"

# load pparg target files
pparg_predicted <- rio::import(here::here(datadir,"PPARG_prediction.csv"), trust = TRUE)
pparg_verified <- rio::import(here::here(datadir,"PPARG.xlsx"), trust = TRUE)


# select high and medium confidence genes from predicted pparg target file
pparg_predicted_filtered <- pparg_predicted %>%
  filter(pparg_predicted$`confidence class` %in% c("high confidence", "medium confidence")) %>%
  pull(GeneSymbol) %>%
  unique()

# select mouse species genes from verified pparg target file
pparg_verified_filtered <- pparg_verified %>%
  filter(Species == "mouse") %>%
  dplyr::select(GeneSymbol = Gene_symbol)
class(pparg_verified)
# rename gene column
pparg_verified_filtered <- data.frame(GeneSymbol = pparg_verified_filtered)


### get overlapping genes and calculate percentage or verified genes ###

# function for overlapping genes and percent
get_overlap <- function(gene_list, deg_list) {
  overlap <- intersect(gene_list, deg_list)
  percent <- count(overlap) / count(deg_list) * 100
  list(overlap = overlap, percent = percent)}

# match verified genes to DEG intersections -  no overlaps with the verified geneset
res_12_verified <- get_overlap(pparg_verified_filtered, common_intersection_12)
res_80_verified <- get_overlap(pparg_verified_filtered, treatment_DEGs_unique_80)
res_92_verified <- get_overlap(pparg_verified_filtered, treatment_DEGs_92)

res_verified <- cbind(res_12_verified, res_80_verified, res_92_verified)
res_verified <- data.frame(GeneSymbol = unlist(res_verified))


human_entrez_all <- AnnotationDbi::select(
  org.Hs.eg.db,
  keys = unique(pparg_predicted$GeneSymbol),
  columns = c("ENTREZID"),
  keytype = "SYMBOL")
# check for NA
human_entrez_all %>% 
  dplyr::filter(is.na(ENTREZID))
human_entrez_all <- human_entrez_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(ENTREZID))

pparg_predicted_filtered <- orthogene::convert_orthologs(
  gene_df = human_entrez_all,
  gene_input = "SYMBOL",
  gene_output = "columns",
  input_species = "human",
  output_species = "mouse",
  method = "homologene", 
  non121_strategy = "keep_popular")

# mouse symbols as data frame with column GeneSymbol
pparg_predicted_filtered <- data.frame(GeneSymbol = unique(pparg_predicted_filtered$ortholog_gene))


### get overlapping genes and calculate percentage ###
# match verified genes to DEG intersections -  no overlaps with the verified geneset
res_12_predicted <- get_overlap(pparg_predicted_filtered, common_intersection_12)
res_80_predicted <- get_overlap(pparg_predicted_filtered, treatment_DEGs_unique_80)
res_92_predicted <- get_overlap(pparg_predicted_filtered, treatment_DEGs_92)

res_predicted <- cbind(res_12_predicted, res_80_predicted, res_92_predicted)
res_predicted <- data.frame(GeneSymbol = unlist(res_predicted))

# export results
res_verified %>%
  rio::export(here::here(resultsdir, "res_verified.RDS")) 
res_verified %>%
  rio::export(here::here(resultsdir, "res_verified.xlsx")) 

res_predicted %>%
  rio::export(here::here(resultsdir, "res_predicted.RDS")) 
res_predicted %>%
  rio::export(here::here(resultsdir, "res_predicted.xlsx"))

### get pie charts of percentages of overlapping PPARG target genes ###

# plot function
plot_overlap_pie <- function(overlap_df, deg_df, title) {
  
  n_overlap <- nrow(overlap_df)
  n_total <- nrow(deg_df)
  
  df <- data.frame(
    group = c("PPARG target", "Other DEGs"),
    count = c(n_overlap, n_total - n_overlap))
  
  df$percent <- round(df$count / sum(df$count) * 100, 1)
  
  ggplot(df, aes(x = "", y = count, fill = group)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1, color = "white", alpha = 0.9) +
    coord_polar("y") +
    theme_void() +
    labs(title = title, fill = NULL) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = paste0(percent, "%")),
      position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
      size = 8) +
    geom_bar(
      stat = "identity", 
      width = 1, 
      color = "grey60", 
      linewidth = 0.2, 
      alpha = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("PPARG target" = "#FBF3B9", 
                                "Other DEGs" = "#FFDCCC")) + 
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = -15), size = 15),
      panel.background = element_blank()) +

    annotate("path",
             x = 1.5,
             y = seq(0, sum(df$count), length.out = 100),
             color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3)}


# plots for predicted PPARG Targets #

# overlapping pie charts - 12
pie_12_predicted <- plot_overlap_pie(overlap_df = res_12_predicted$overlap,
                                     deg_df = common_intersection_12,
                                     title = "PPARG pred targets in DEGs - contrast 12")
plot(pie_12_predicted)
# check for validity
nrow(res_12_predicted$overlap) <= nrow(common_intersection_12)
all(res_12_predicted$overlap$GeneSymbol %in% common_intersection_12$GeneSymbol)
ggsave("Pie_PPARG_pred_targets_12.tiff", pie_12_predicted, dpi = 600)
```
